messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx/429 rate detected on api.redwood-inference/v1/generate and /v1/embeddings starting 13:24 UTC. Symptoms: increased tail latency, kernel queue growth, and client-facing 429s. Paging on-call: @Sam-O, @Liam-SRE, @Maya-SDK.

Sam-O: I'm oncall, looking at graphs now. Root causes look like a mix of large embedding batch jobs + a few streaming chat clients keeping long-lived connections and starving slots.

Liam-SRE: Confirmed. Host-level GPU queue depth >90% on 3 clusters. Logs show repeated `rpc: deadline exceeded` and `resource unavailable` from runtime. A couple of customers are sending 50+ parallel long-stream sessions.

Sam-O: Quick mitigation suggestions (what I can enact now):
- soft per-customer concurrency caps for top offenders (reduce allowed concurrent requests by 60% for 5 offending orgs)
- apply temporary routing rule to divert new requests from heavy customers to smaller model variant (faster, cheaper, less kv pressure)
- disable streaming responses for the embeddings endpoint for hosted customers (fall back to single response)
- if still overloaded, flip an emergency feature flag to reject >X tokens/batch with 429 + Retry-After

Liam-SRE: +1. I'll push the concurrency caps and routing rule now. Command (internal):
```
PATCH /internal/traffic-shaper
{ "action": "set_soft_cap", "orgs": ["org-123","org-456","org-789"], "cap": 0.4 }
```
This should immediately shed the most pressure.

Maya-SDK: SDK team — we need to publish client-side mitigation guidance immediately so customers can reduce retries and avoid amplifying load. Draft guidance below — please review and publish to status and SDK quickfix.

Maya-SDK: ADVISORY DRAFT (short):
- If you receive 429 or 503 from Redwood, stop aggressive retries. Implement exponential backoff with full jitter.
- Respect `Retry-After` header from the API and prefer server-provided backoff windows when present.
- For idempotent requests (embedding, stateless generate with an idempotency key), retry with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts. For non-idempotent requests, retry at most once after confirming user intent.
- If you use streaming (server-sent tokens/streams), provide an option to fall back to non-streaming (single response) to reduce connection overhead.

Maya-SDK: Example JS snippet for exponential backoff + jitter:
```
// full jitter exponential backoff
async function retry(fn, maxAttempts = 6, baseMs = 100) {
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (err) {
      const isRetryable = err.status === 429 || err.status === 503 || err.code === 'ETIMEDOUT';
      if (!isRetryable || attempt === maxAttempts) throw err;
      const maxDelay = Math.min(10000, baseMs * 2 ** attempt);
      const delay = Math.random() * maxDelay; // full jitter
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, delay));
    }
  }
}
```

Maya-SDK: Example Python idempotency header guidance:
```
# include an Idempotency-Key for requests that change state or are safe to retry
headers = {"Idempotency-Key": "<uuid-v4>", "Authorization": "Bearer ..."}
# clients should generate a new key per logical operation, not per attempt
```

Maya-SDK: For streaming -> non-streaming fallback (JS):
```
// SDK option
client.request({ streaming: false, model: 'gpt-medium', prompt })
// fallback if streaming connections are rejected or latency spikes
```

Sam-O: Good. Add explicit recommended values for customers we contact: base backoff 100ms, max backoff 10s, max attempts 5 for idempotent ops, respect Retry-After always, add jitter. Also advise they reduce concurrency to 5-10 parallel requests per client instance.

Nora-PM: I'll coordinate comms for the top 10 impacted customers. Support should start live outreach with suggested settings and offer assistance switching to smaller model variants or non-streaming mode.

Liam-SRE: Live actions taken: applied soft caps, started routing rule, disabled embeddings streaming for hosted. Early telemetry: GPU queue depth dropping, 5xx rate reduced by ~45% over last 3m.

ops-bot: Deploy log: traffic-shaper v2.3 applied to org-123, org-456, org-789 @ 13:33 UTC — change_id: ts-2191234580.

Sam-O: Maya, can SDK push a patched minor release with the backoff util and a short note in release notes? Also post the advisory to status.redwood and our #status page.

Maya-SDK: Yes — releasing 0.12.4 patch with `retryWithJitter()` and `idempotency` header helpers in ~20m. Draft status update: "We have applied server-side throttles to mitigate elevated error rates. To reduce the likelihood of client-side retries worsening congestion, we recommend implementing exponential backoff with full jitter, honoring Retry-After, using idempotency keys for safe retries, and providing a non-streaming fallback."

Sam-O: Support thread created for top customers and docs link will be attached to that thread. I'll keep watching graphs and will update here in 10m.

Liam-SRE: Follow-up: if we see a rebound after easing caps, plan B is to escalate to circuit-breaker that returns 503 for >X connections per org and block new streaming sessions until pressure subsides.

Sam-O: Noted. Current status: mitigations holding, continue monitoring.

ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigations applied @ 13:33 UTC, monitoring.

Sam-O: I'll close this thread once error rate is stable <0.5% for 15m.

Maya-SDK: Published advisory + SDK patch to staging, will push to prod after smoke tests.

Nora-PM: Thanks all — great triage. Keep customer comms tight.

Sam-O: Update @ 13:51 UTC: 5xx down to baseline, latency improving. Leaving soft caps in place for 30m then gradually roll back.

ops-bot: incident-bot: resolved -> monitors green at 13:52 UTC.
